rationale: C02 is the immediately preceding annual Flag Day proclamation and supplies the child's central drafting structure and concrete operative machinery: commemoration of the flag's June 14, 1777 adoption, public display of the flag at homes or other suitable places, and governmental display on public buildings. The child updates the year, incorporates the new 1949 congressional resolution, and rearranges the governmental and public calls, but retains materially parallel language and provisions. C22 is an earlier version of substantially the same annual template, while C11 shares the flag-display subject but concerns a distinct permanent rule for Fort McHenry.

shared_material.child_excerpt: observe that day as the anniversary of the adoption on June 14, 1777, by the Continental Congress, of the Stars and Stripes as the official flag of the United States of America
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the American flag ... was adopted by the Continental Congress on June 14, 1777
shared_material.explanation: Both recitals and operative language center the annual observance on the same adoption event and date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: by flying the flag at their homes or other suitable places
shared_material.parent_excerpt: honor our colors by displaying them at their homes or other suitable places
shared_material.explanation: This is a close and distinctive reuse of the public-display instruction.

shared_material.child_excerpt: call upon the appropriate officials of the Federal Government, and of the State and local Governments, to arrange for the display of the flag of our Republic on all public buildings on Flag Day
shared_material.parent_excerpt: direct the appropriate officials of the Government to display the flag of the United States on all Government buildings on Flag Day
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts the same governmental flag-display provision while expanding the officials and buildings covered.
